forTheCaptain: The determination's premise held. The committed track registry does hold the filing destination for both families, in destination.name, destination.detail and venue, so nothing was reversed and no guess was substituted.

One scope note: the verifier's smallestExactRepair said the repair lay 'neither in the rendered legal text'. Two sentences of rendered legal text did change - the motion now states the destination and that no filing fee is charged, and the certificate of service now names who must be served. Both are read from the same registry entry as the destination, and leaving them would have had the packet state the destination while asserting one line up that the service party and the fee were unestablished. A Captain may prefer the narrower repair; if so, the SERVICE and FEE_AND_WAIVER sentences are the ones to pull back, and FILING_DESTINATION and ROUTE_IDENTITY stand alone without them.

This host was not build-deterministic before this repair, which no lane had recorded. The fix was to adopt the factory's existing stampDeterministic helper. Other hosts that create a packet container with PDFDocument.create() and save with updateMetadata:false may carry the same defect and would silently invalidate their own raster receipts on every rebuild; that is worth a sweep by a lane that owns it, and this worker did not go looking outside its two families.
A fresh raster is owed for all four fixtures, and a fresh independent verification read is owed for both families. This worker released both lanes and verified nothing of its own.
